target_customer: D2C brands and content creators in Indonesia
problem: Creators and D2C brands in Indonesia lack business accounts and working capital because lenders treat them as informal or risky.
business_model: Fintech: invoice financing with an admin fee of 1.8 to 2.5 percent per month plus account and software features
product_category: Creator and D2C fintech, business banking and financing

founders.name: Wafa Taftazani
founders.background_notes: YC bio cites 10+ years across technology, digital entertainment, corporate finance, public policy and international relations; no employers named.

competitors.name: BintanGO
competitors.what: Invoice financing and tools for Indonesian creators
competitors.traction_then: Reported by TechCrunch in April 2022 as targeting creators without access to credit

technical_complexity.rationale: Lending, bank partnership and compliance in Indonesia are mostly operational and regulatory; the software itself is standard fintech engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Licensing helps a little, but credit scoring on creator income was not proven and rivals like BintanGO targeted the same group.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move found. The Ken later reported only 300 to 500 monthly active users and questioned the 120M valuation claim.

market_need_then: The company claims over 700,000 D2C brands and creators in Indonesia and a 14B dollar a year opportunity (company figures, unverified). TechCrunch notes creators are often classed as informal workers and struggle to get credit.

identity.voice_and_tone: Creator-friendly, positions as Brex for creators

branding.brand_signature: Celebrity investors Raffi Ahmad and Nagita Slavina used in coverage
branding.community_and_virality: Indonesian press coverage of the round spotlighted celebrity creator investors; one site claim of fastest to centaur status is unverified.

brand_strength.rationale: Press attention came from celebrity investors and the valuation claim, but usage stayed small per The Ken.

outcome_analysis: UpBanx raised a 5.2M dollar pre-seed in January 2022 with celebrity creators and Alpha JWC, claimed a 120M dollar valuation, then reportedly had only 300 to 500 monthly active users per The Ken. Its site now stresses invoice financing and an AI copy tool, which points to a narrowed focus. No shutdown found, so the outcome is unresolved and traction looks weak.
notes: YC page says 5.6M raised in total; CB Insights says 5.7M; the January 2022 round was 5.2M per FinTech Global and DealStreetAsia (second outlet seen only in a search snippet). The 120M valuation is the company's own claim and was not recorded as post-money. The Ken article date unknown; the weak traction claim comes from the search snippet only and failure factor weak_willingness_to_pay is tentative. BintanGO source is dated after the batch start (about one month after the W22 batch). DailySocial pages returned 503. Company site claims product shift to invoice financing and UpThinx AI tool, undated. No dated pre-batch competitor was found.
